name: Plurality
moduleIntroduction: Welcome to Plurality! This module is about how to make nouns singular (one) or plural (more than one). In spoken French, the plural 's' is usually silent, but in English, it is almost always pronounced. Also, words like 'information' and 'advice' are uncountable in English—they never take an 's'. We will practice these differences to avoid common mistakes.
contrastiveExplanation:
Regular Plurals:
English: Add '-s' and pronounce it (Book -> Books).
French: Add '-s' but it is silent (Livre -> Livres).

Irregular Plurals:
English: Man -> Men, Person -> People, Child -> Children.
French: Usually regular (Homme -> Hommes).

Uncountable Nouns:
English: Information, Advice, Furniture, Luggage, Homework (Always Singular).
French: Des informations, des conseils, des meubles (Plural).
